quests.hint: This verb means to officially make a formal, solemn commitment or declaration.
quests.explanation: 'Avow support,' 'avow a belief,' and 'avowed purpose' are key. 'Avow' is formal and implies public declaration. 'Avowed' as an adjective means openly acknowledged: 'avowed opponent.'
quests.textToSpeak: She publicly ___ her commitment to democratic principles and the rule of law.
quests.correctAnswer: She publicly avowed her commitment to democratic principles and the rule of law.

quests.hint: This verb means to give up a formal claim or right, especially in writing.
quests.explanation: 'Renounce citizenship,' 'renounce a claim,' and 'renounce violence' are key. 'Renunciation' is the noun. Stronger and more formal than 'give up.' Often used in political or legal contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: He chose to ___ his inheritance rather than accept the conditions attached to it.
quests.correctAnswer: He chose to renounce his inheritance rather than accept the conditions attached to it.

quests.hint: This verb means to formally withdraw from a treaty, agreement, or position.
quests.explanation: 'Repudiate a claim,' 'repudiate an agreement,' and 'repudiation of' are key. 'Repudiation' is the noun. Stronger than 'reject' - it implies refusing any obligation or responsibility.
quests.textToSpeak: The new government ___ the treaty signed by its predecessor, citing changed circumstances.
quests.correctAnswer: The new government repudiated the treaty signed by its predecessor, citing changed circumstances.

quests.hint: This verb means to formally oppose a motion, proposal, or decision in a meeting.
quests.explanation: 'Veto a proposal,' 'exercise a veto,' and 'right of veto' are key. 'Veto' is both noun and verb. The UN Security Council permanent members each have veto power over resolutions.
quests.textToSpeak: The United States threatened to ___ any Security Council resolution that named the country.
quests.correctAnswer: The United States threatened to veto any Security Council resolution that named the country.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially agree to or take upon yourself a duty, expense, or risk.
quests.explanation: 'Assume responsibility,' 'assume the burden,' and 'assume control' are key. 'Assumption' (noun) means taking on something, or a belief accepted as true. Context determines meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: By signing the contract, the contractor agreed to ___ full liability for any damage caused.
quests.correctAnswer: By signing the contract, the contractor agreed to assume full liability for any damage caused.

quests.hint: This verb means to formally accept and take on a commitment or duty.
quests.explanation: 'Undertake a task,' 'undertake research,' and 'I undertake to' are key. 'Undertaking' (noun) means a formal promise or commitment. 'Funeral undertaker' is an entirely unrelated use.
quests.textToSpeak: She agreed to ___ the project with the proviso that adequate funding would be made available.
quests.correctAnswer: She agreed to undertake the project with the proviso that adequate funding would be made available.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a condition or qualification attached to an agreement or undertaking.
quests.explanation: 'With the proviso that,' 'subject to the proviso,' and 'one important proviso' are key. 'Proviso' is stronger than 'condition' - it is built into the agreement itself.
quests.textToSpeak: He accepted the offer with the ___ that his title and responsibilities would remain unchanged.
quests.correctAnswer: He accepted the offer with the proviso that his title and responsibilities would remain unchanged.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a principle or understanding that is accepted without being written down.
quests.explanation: 'An unwritten rule,' 'an unwritten convention,' and 'by convention' are key. 'Convention' also means a large formal meeting. 'Conventional' means following accepted norms or standards.
quests.textToSpeak: By ___, the most senior minister chairs the meeting in the absence of the prime minister.
quests.correctAnswer: By convention, the most senior minister chairs the meeting in the absence of the prime minister.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the principles that define what is and is not allowable in a particular field.
quests.explanation: 'The bounds of,' 'within the bounds of,' and 'push the boundaries' are key. 'Out of bounds' means outside what is permitted. 'Boundary conditions' define the scope of something.
quests.textToSpeak: The research team worked hard to stay clearly within the ethical ___ set by the committee.
quests.correctAnswer: The research team worked hard to stay clearly within the ethical bounds set by the committee.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially take back something that was previously given or stated.
quests.explanation: 'Retract a statement,' 'retract an allegation,' and 'retraction' are key. 'Retract' (verb) and 'retraction' (noun) are used in law and journalism when false claims are withdrawn.
quests.textToSpeak: The newspaper was ordered to ___ the story and publish a front-page correction.
quests.correctAnswer: The newspaper was ordered to retract the story and publish a front-page correction.

quests.hint: This verb means to make a public apology or correction for a previous false statement.
quests.explanation: 'Issue a disclaimer,' 'publish a disclaimer,' and 'disclaimer of responsibility' are key. 'Disclaimer' is also a legal statement limiting liability. 'Disclaim' means to deny responsibility.
quests.textToSpeak: The company published a ___ stating that its earlier announcement had contained inaccurate figures.
quests.correctAnswer: The company published a disclaimer stating that its earlier announcement had contained inaccurate figures.

quests.hint: This verb means to deny or formally dispute something that has been attributed to you.
quests.explanation: 'Disavow a statement,' 'disavow responsibility,' and 'publicly disavowed' are key. 'Disavowal' is the noun. Stronger and more deliberate than 'deny.' Implies a formal repudiation.
quests.textToSpeak: The minister quickly ___ the comments made by her party colleague at the conference.
quests.correctAnswer: The minister quickly disavowed the comments made by her party colleague at the conference.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the act of moving ownership, rights, or possession from one party to another.
quests.explanation: 'Transfer of ownership,' 'transfer rights,' and 'asset transfer' are key. 'Transfer' is both noun and verb. Used widely in legal, financial, and sporting contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ of the patent to a new owner required the approval of the licensing board.
quests.correctAnswer: The transfer of the patent to a new owner required the approval of the licensing board.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the authority given to one person to act legally on behalf of another.
quests.explanation: 'Power of attorney,' 'grant a power of attorney,' and 'act under power of attorney' are key. 'Attorney' means a legal representative - used both in law and as a job title.
quests.textToSpeak: She was granted ___ of attorney to manage her elderly father's financial affairs.
quests.correctAnswer: She was granted power of attorney to manage her elderly father's financial affairs.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a formal written order from a court requiring or preventing something.
quests.explanation: 'Injunction against,' 'seek an injunction,' and 'temporary injunction' are key. 'Injunct' is the verb. An injunction is a powerful legal tool used to stop harmful actions immediately.
quests.textToSpeak: The company obtained a court ___ preventing the former employee from sharing trade secrets.
quests.correctAnswer: The company obtained a court injunction preventing the former employee from sharing trade secrets.

quests.hint: This noun refers to formal official notice that an agreement will end at a specified time.
quests.explanation: 'Serve notice,' 'give notice,' and 'notice period' are key. 'Notice' in employment means the period before leaving a job. 'Notice to quit' is a formal legal document.
quests.textToSpeak: The landlord served three months' ___ on the commercial tenant citing repeated lease violations.
quests.correctAnswer: The landlord served three months' notice on the commercial tenant citing repeated lease violations.

quests.hint: This noun refers to money paid to make up for loss, damage, or harm suffered.
quests.explanation: 'Financial compensation,' 'seek compensation,' and 'compensation claim' are key. 'Compensate' is the verb. Often used in legal contexts involving damages awarded to a claimant.
quests.textToSpeak: The defendants agreed to pay ___ of two million pounds to end the class action.
quests.correctAnswer: The defendants agreed to pay compensation of two million pounds to end the class action.

quests.hint: This noun refers to an official order requiring someone to appear in court or produce evidence.
quests.explanation: 'Issue a subpoena,' 'receive a subpoena,' and 'under subpoena' are key. 'Subpoena' (from Latin) compels someone to appear or produce documents. Failure to comply is contempt.
quests.textToSpeak: The journalist received a ___ requiring him to reveal the source of his confidential information.
quests.correctAnswer: The journalist received a subpoena requiring him to reveal the source of his confidential information.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the legal right to pursue a claim against another party for compensation.
quests.explanation: 'Legal recourse,' 'have recourse to,' and 'without recourse' are key. 'Have recourse to the law' means to use legal processes. 'Without recourse' means accepting risk without future claim.
quests.textToSpeak: Customers who received defective products have full legal ___ against the manufacturer.
quests.correctAnswer: Customers who received defective products have full legal recourse against the manufacturer.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the decision in a legal case about whether someone is guilty.
quests.explanation: 'Return a verdict,' 'unanimous verdict,' and 'verdict of not guilty' are key. 'Verdict' is from Latin: 'vere dictum' meaning 'truly said.' The jury delivers the verdict; the judge passes sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: After three days of deliberation, the jury returned a ___ of not guilty on all counts.
quests.correctAnswer: After three days of deliberation, the jury returned a verdict of not guilty on all counts.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the punishment formally given by a judge to a convicted person.
quests.explanation: 'Pass a sentence,' 'serve a sentence,' and 'suspended sentence' are key. 'Sentence' is both noun and verb: 'to sentence someone.' 'Commute a sentence' means to reduce it.
quests.textToSpeak: The judge passed a ___ of five years, noting the defendant's previous clean record.
quests.correctAnswer: The judge passed a sentence of five years, noting the defendant's previous clean record.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the act of calling someone to account and requiring explanation.
quests.explanation: 'Reckoning will come,' 'a day of reckoning,' and 'bring someone to reckoning' are key. 'Reckoning' can also mean calculation. 'Dead reckoning' is navigation by calculation without landmarks.
quests.textToSpeak: The financial crisis brought a ___ for the reckless lending practices of the previous decade.
quests.correctAnswer: The financial crisis brought a reckoning for the reckless lending practices of the previous decade.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the system of values and beliefs that a person or society uses to judge right and wrong.
quests.explanation: 'Moral framework,' 'moral compass,' and 'question the morality of' are key. 'Moral' as an adjective: 'a moral decision.' 'Morality' as an abstract noun refers to the system of ethics.
quests.textToSpeak: The decision raised serious questions about the ___ of prioritising profit over human welfare.
quests.correctAnswer: The decision raised serious questions about the morality of prioritising profit over human welfare.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the most honest and transparent account of something - the full, unmodified truth.
quests.explanation: 'The unvarnished truth,' 'speak plainly,' and 'give the unvarnished facts' are key. 'Varnish' covers and beautifies surfaces. 'Unvarnished' means without any softening or embellishment.
quests.textToSpeak: She appreciated his ___ assessment of the situation, however uncomfortable it was to hear.
quests.correctAnswer: She appreciated his unvarnished assessment of the situation, however uncomfortable it was to hear.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the period before a new law, policy, or system formally begins.
quests.explanation: 'Before the law takes effect,' 'prior to enactment,' and 'the run-up to' - but specifically 'preamble.' 'Preamble' is the introductory statement before a law, often outlining its purpose.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ to the constitution sets out the foundational values the legal system is built upon.
quests.correctAnswer: The preamble to the constitution sets out the foundational values the legal system is built upon.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a principle or accepted belief that most people in a field agree on.
quests.explanation: 'Scientific consensus,' 'the prevailing orthodoxy,' and 'challenge orthodoxy' are key. 'Orthodoxy' means the accepted mainstream view. 'Orthodox' is the adjective. 'Unorthodox' challenges it.
quests.textToSpeak: The paper directly challenged the prevailing ___ on how language is acquired in early childhood.
quests.correctAnswer: The paper directly challenged the prevailing orthodoxy on how language is acquired in early childhood.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the deeply ingrained attitudes and assumptions shared within a society.
quests.explanation: 'Cultural mentality,' 'collective mentality,' and 'change the mentality' are key. 'Mentality' refers to a characteristic way of thinking. 'Siege mentality' means feeling besieged or under constant threat.
quests.textToSpeak: Shifting the public ___ around mental health requires sustained effort over many years.
quests.correctAnswer: Shifting the public mentality around mental health requires sustained effort over many years.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the most essential and defining characteristic that makes something what it is.
quests.explanation: 'The essence of,' 'in essence,' and 'capture the essence' are key. 'Essential' is derived from 'essence.' 'In essence' means fundamentally or stripped to its core. 'Quintessence' is the purest form.
quests.textToSpeak: At its ___, great leadership is simply the art of helping others do their very best work.
quests.correctAnswer: At its essence, great leadership is simply the art of helping others do their very best work.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the final, highest point of skill, development, or refinement in something.
quests.explanation: 'The pinnacle of achievement,' 'reach the pinnacle,' and 'at the pinnacle of their career' are key. 'Pinnacle' suggests the very top. Originally referred to a small turret at the top of a building.
quests.textToSpeak: She reached the absolute ___ of her profession when she was appointed to the international court.
quests.correctAnswer: She reached the absolute pinnacle of her profession when she was appointed to the international court.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the full, ideal realisation of a potential or effort - its most complete form.
quests.explanation: 'Culmination of efforts,' 'the culmination of,' and 'reach its culmination' are key. 'Culminate' is the verb. A culmination is the final, crowning point that a long process builds toward.
quests.textToSpeak: Her final lecture was the ___ of forty years of research, teaching, and passionate advocacy.
quests.correctAnswer: Her final lecture was the culmination of forty years of research, teaching, and passionate advocacy.
